title: Shift Distance Between Two Strings
summary: Given two strings s and t of the same length, and two integer arrays nextCost and previousCost , you can perform operations on any character s[i] to shift it to the next or previous letter in the alphabet.
statement: Given two strings s and t of the same length, and two integer arrays nextCost and previousCost , you can perform operations on any character s[i] to shift it to the next or previous letter in the alphabet. If s[i] is 'z', it wraps to 'a', and if s[i] is 'a', it wraps to 'z'. The cost of shifting s[i] to the next letter is given by nextCost[j] , where j is the position of s[i] in the alphabet. Similarly, the cost of shifting s[i] to the previous letter is given by previousCost[j] . The shift distance is the minimum total cost required to transform s into t . Return this shift distance.
constraints: s and t have the same length up to 100,000; both cost arrays contain 26 nonnegative values.
Moving forward from letter j costs next_cost[j]; moving backward from j costs previous_cost[j], with alphabet wraparound.
Return the sum of the cheaper directional route for every independent character position.
reference_solution:
def minimum_cyclic_shift_cost(s,t,next_cost,previous_cost):
    forward=[0]*53;backward=[0]*53
    for index in range(52):
        forward[index+1]=forward[index]+next_cost[index%26]
        backward[index+1]=backward[index]+previous_cost[(index+1)%26]
    answer=0
    for source,target in zip(s,t):
        a=ord(source)-97;b=ord(target)-97
        clockwise=forward[b+26 if b<a else b]-forward[a]
        counter=backward[a+26 if a<b else a]-backward[b]
        answer+=min(clockwise,counter)
    return answer
